definitions.label: O
definitions.name: O-Type Star
definitions.tooltip: An O-type star is an exceptionally hot, massive, blue star. Its classification comes from its spectrum, and its short lifetime and intense ultraviolet output strongly affect its surroundings.
definitions.short_tooltip: An exceptionally hot, massive blue star.

definitions.label: B
definitions.name: B-Type Star
definitions.tooltip: A B-type star is a hot, luminous blue-white star whose spectrum indicates a high surface temperature and relatively short stellar lifetime.

definitions.label: A
definitions.name: A-Type Star
definitions.tooltip: An A-type star is a hot white or blue-white star. Its spectrum is dominated by strong hydrogen absorption lines.
definitions.short_tooltip: A hot white or blue-white star.

definitions.label: F
definitions.name: F-Type Star
definitions.tooltip: An F-type star is a yellow-white star hotter and generally more massive than the Sun, with a greater share of ultraviolet output.
definitions.short_tooltip: A yellow-white star hotter than the Sun.

definitions.label: G
definitions.name: G-Type Star
definitions.tooltip: A G-type star is a yellow-white star in the same broad spectral class as the Sun. Spectral class describes temperature and absorption features, not habitability.

definitions.label: K
definitions.name: K-Type Star
definitions.tooltip: A K-type star is an orange star cooler and usually longer-lived than the Sun. Its spectral class alone does not determine age or planetary conditions.

definitions.label: M
definitions.name: M-Type Star
definitions.tooltip: An M-type star is a cool red stellar class. Many are small, long-lived red dwarfs, while evolved red giants can also have M-type spectra.

definitions.label: L
definitions.name: L-Type Ultracool Object
definitions.tooltip: An L-type ultracool object has an atmosphere cool enough for metal hydrides and condensate clouds. The class includes both very low-mass stars and brown dwarfs.

definitions.label: T
definitions.name: T-Type Brown Dwarf
definitions.tooltip: A T-type brown dwarf is a cool substellar object whose near-infrared spectrum commonly shows strong methane absorption.
definitions.short_tooltip: A cool methane-bearing brown dwarf class.

definitions.label: Y
definitions.name: Y-Type Brown Dwarf
definitions.tooltip: A Y-type brown dwarf belongs to the coldest recognized brown-dwarf spectral class and is detected primarily through infrared observations.

definitions.label: WR
definitions.name: Wolf-Rayet Star
definitions.tooltip: A Wolf-Rayet star is a hot, evolved massive star with broad emission lines and powerful winds that expose chemically processed material.
definitions.short_tooltip: A hot evolved star with powerful winds.

definitions.label: WD
definitions.name: White Dwarf
definitions.tooltip: A white dwarf is a compact stellar remnant supported by electron degeneracy pressure. It no longer sustains ordinary stellar fusion and cools over time.

definitions.label: NS
definitions.name: Neutron Star
definitions.tooltip: A neutron star is the compact remnant left by some core-collapse supernovae, compressing more than a solar mass into a city-sized object.

definitions.label: PULSAR
definitions.name: Pulsar
definitions.tooltip: A pulsar is a rotating neutron star observed through periodic beams of electromagnetic radiation.
definitions.short_tooltip: A periodically observed rotating neutron star.

definitions.label: MAGNETAR
definitions.name: Magnetar
definitions.tooltip: A magnetar is a neutron star whose observed behavior is powered in large part by an exceptionally strong magnetic field.
definitions.short_tooltip: A neutron star with an extreme magnetic field.

definitions.label: BH
definitions.name: Stellar-Mass Black Hole
definitions.tooltip: A stellar-mass black hole is a compact remnant whose gravity produces an event horizon. Spacegate applies this tag only when accepted compact-object evidence supports it.

definitions.label: 1 Known Star
definitions.name: One Known Stellar Member
definitions.tooltip: Spacegate currently has one accepted stellar member in this system. This is not proof that no undiscovered or unresolved companion exists.
definitions.short_tooltip: One accepted stellar member; unseen companions may exist.

definitions.label: Binary
definitions.name: Binary Star System
definitions.tooltip: This accepted Spacegate hierarchy contains two stellar members. The tag describes accepted membership, not whether every orbital element is known.

definitions.label: Multiple
definitions.name: Multiple Star System
definitions.tooltip: This accepted Spacegate hierarchy contains at least three stellar members.
definitions.short_tooltip: Three or more accepted stellar members.

definitions.label: Hierarchical
definitions.name: Hierarchical Multiple System
definitions.tooltip: The accepted hierarchy organizes three or more stellar members into nested groups. The tag describes structure and does not by itself certify long-term dynamical stability.
definitions.short_tooltip: Stellar members are organized into nested groups.

definitions.label: Planet Host
definitions.name: Confirmed Planet Host
definitions.tooltip: At least one confirmed canonical planet is linked to this system. Candidate-only evidence does not activate this tag.
definitions.short_tooltip: Hosts at least one confirmed planet.

definitions.label: USP
definitions.name: Ultra-Short-Period Planet
definitions.tooltip: This confirmed planet has a selected orbital period shorter than one day. The tag follows the conventional ultra-short-period screening threshold.
definitions.short_tooltip: A confirmed planet orbiting in under one day.

definitions.label: HZ Screen
definitions.name: Habitable-Zone Screening Signal
definitions.tooltip: A broad temperature or insolation screen places at least one confirmed planet near a modeled habitable-zone range. This is not a claim that the planet is habitable.
definitions.short_tooltip: A broad habitable-zone screen, not a habitability claim.

definitions.label: Nearby
definitions.name: Nearby System
definitions.tooltip: This system is within 25 light-years of Sol using Spacegate's selected distance.

definitions.label: Local Neighborhood
definitions.name: Local Stellar Neighborhood
definitions.tooltip: This system is more than 25 and no more than 100 light-years from Sol using Spacegate's selected distance.

definitions.label: Hot Jupiter
definitions.name: Hot Gas Giant
definitions.tooltip: A confirmed planet classified by Spacegate's versioned broad map policy as both gas-giant-like and hot.

definitions.label: Temperate Jupiter
definitions.name: Temperate Gas Giant
definitions.tooltip: A confirmed planet classified by Spacegate's versioned broad map policy as gas-giant-like with temperate irradiation.

definitions.label: Cold Jupiter
definitions.name: Cold Gas Giant
definitions.tooltip: A confirmed planet classified by Spacegate's versioned broad map policy as both gas-giant-like and cold.

definitions.label: Hot Terrestrial
definitions.name: Hot Terrestrial Planet
definitions.tooltip: A confirmed planet classified by Spacegate's versioned broad map policy as terrestrial-size or terrestrial-mass and hot.

definitions.label: Temperate Terrestrial
definitions.name: Temperate Terrestrial Planet
definitions.tooltip: A confirmed planet classified by Spacegate's broad map policy as terrestrial-scale with temperate irradiation. This does not establish surface conditions or habitability.

definitions.label: Cold Terrestrial
definitions.name: Cold Terrestrial Planet
definitions.tooltip: A confirmed planet classified by Spacegate's versioned broad map policy as terrestrial-scale and cold.
